goal: Replace the flat specialist skill lists with a composed, discoverable, DSH-native skill layer: verified frontmatter, tiered core/specialist/capability composition, find-activate-load discovery wired to DSH invalidation, and a correct provider contract.

alignment.evidence: Feature branch feature/skill-architecture-v2; Project Harness reusable harness only, no product code and no live DSH session.

Read the DSH skill subsystem doc and source (registry, tool-skill catalogue rendering, filesystem provider frontmatter, ranks, invalidation, watcher) plus the current adapter, presets and 25-skill library before editing.
00-PLANNING/SKILL-ARCHITECTURE-V2.md models the gap: fixed flat required_skills, H1-derived descriptions, no invalidation, no discovery path, config- rather than cwd-sensitive resolution.
Skill layer only. One new bounded write (.harness/state/skills.json on activation). No shell, no Git mutation, no merge, release, deployment or live provider call.
DSH owns the registry, layering and catalogue rendering; dsh/skills/*.js owns composition, discovery and plan resolution; capabilities.json owns the vocabulary; each skill owns its own frontmatter.

Phase one only: normalise metadata, replace required_skills with core/specialist/capability composition, add find-activate discovery and correct the provider. Native .dsh/skills migration and new specialists are explicitly out of scope.

Node built-ins only, no new dependency; bounded walks and reads; path containment on reads and the single write; atomic write; stat-poll instead of a chokidar dependency; stray non-skill entry and duplicate preset filename removed.

Node 22.23.2: 80/80 tests including 31 new frontmatter, library, composition, activation, provider-contract and invalidation tests; skills:verify, control:verify, memory:resume and git diff --check passed. Live DSH acceptance remains a separate step.
